proof_attempt_summary: The initialized unknown-damping original-record experiment yields matching coarse minimax risk and honest-length orders plus the consistency threshold, with the informal math and weighted-square citation checks passing. The proposed sharp critical experiments and normalized decision values were not delivered and remain two explicitly disclosed open questions. Independent boundary and main validity audits classify an honest same-topic scope downgrade at incremental tier; the rubric REVISE and minor Liu-Zhong positioning gap remain archived, and no Lean formalization was undertaken.
tldr: The original-record coarse frontier is established for an initialized, slowly relaxing Ornstein--Uhlenbeck switchback with unknown damping and baseline: squared risk has order \(\min\{1,\mathcal S_n^{-1}\}\), and finite-sample honest connected-interval length has order \(\min\{1,\mathcal S_n^{-1/2}\}\). Here \(\mathcal S_n=n\kappa^2\{1-q+\kappa^2\}\). The frontier has an elbow at \(1-q\asymp\kappa^2\): repeat-driven information \(n\kappa^2(1-q)\) and bin-integration leakage \(n\kappa^4\) contribute additively. A candidate-evaluated complete-box likelihood fit attains these orders, with an observable transition-pair fallback. Damping localization and fitted-mean control are proved on the same initialized record. Sharp critical likelihood experiments, oracle-equivalent profiling, and exact positive-information decision constants remain the separate questions posed in the two open-ended statements. The result informs a prospective sustained-effect cadence and logging decision.
gap: Integrated-OU likelihood theory establishes Gaussian observation machinery, and switchback analyses study particular effect estimators or finite-carryover designs. The opened results do not characterize all-procedure treatment risk and honest interval length when a single initialized bin-integral record combines shrinking damping, nearly alternating input and unknown shared mean/covariance nuisance parameters.
fill: Open-ended Question 1 derives the joint initialized experiment and tests oracle-equivalent nuisance profiling. Open-ended Question 2 derives its sharp decision frontier and the uniform transfer needed for original-record risk and coverage. The information theorem exposes the candidate crossover, while the finite-attainment theorem makes the decision benchmark a total, exactly honest procedure. A surviving nuisance channel changes the requested frontier within the same model; it is not removed by a new assumption.
